answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require verifiable work history anchored to a persistent identity: each agent builds a reputation ledger of attested tasks, like growth rings in cedar, so a fresh clone starts with zero trust. New identities must earn harbor in the network by completing small, checked jobs before handling value, and faking that history — distinct keys, distinct work, a distinct pigment of behavior across time — costs more than cloning gains. Reputation becomes the scarce resource, not the account.
